transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-15
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Leo Martinez (Redwood CSM); Evan Park (CTO), Maya Chen (Lead ML Eng), Samira Ortiz (Head Analytics), Ravi Patel (Infra)

Summary:
Redwood + Nova discussion to scope a 6-week POC to validate a production LLM inference integration. Focus areas: success criteria (latency, cost, quality), workload sizing (QPS, concurrency), benchmarks (end-to-end latency, streaming), and integration plan (SDKs, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, function/tool calling, structured output). Action items and timeline captured at the end.

Topics:
- Success criteria and acceptance tests
- Traffic & workload sizing (avg/peak)
- Benchmark plan and metrics dashboard
- Integration choices: Redwood SDKs vs OpenAI-compatible API, function calling, structured responses
- Security: VPC, KMS, SSO, audit logs
- Timeline for 6-week POC and roles

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'll kick us off. We're just gonna run through scope for a POC to validate inference integration, expected traffic, and success criteria. Priya, wanna say hi?
[00:10] Priya Nair: Hi all, yeah excited to dig in. I'll be owning the benchmarks and the technical run through.
[00:15] Evan Park: Thanks. High level
d our goal is to replace a mix of in-house embedding + heuristic reranking with a multi-turn chat + structured extraction flow. We need sub-300ms median token latency in 95th perc for short prompts and 99th under 800ms for the interactive path. Cost has to be predictable; we're budget constrained.
[00:34] Jordan Lee: Got it. When you say interactive path, is that the UI assistants or internal batch pipelines?
[00:40] Samira Ortiz: Both, but primarily UI first. The assistant in our dashboard, users expect near real-time. We also want to run a nightly batch of summarizations, which can be slower.
[00:52] Priya Nair: Ok, so we'll split POC workloads: interactive (low-latency, streaming) and batch (throughput/embeddings). For interactive we recommend a hosted setup to iterate quickly, or Dedicated if you want steady latency and isolation.
[01:08] Maya Chen: Can you clarify tradeoffs? We were also evaluating OpenAI and Anthropic.
[01:12] Jordan Lee: Sure. OpenAI is simple and fast to prototype, but for cost control and VPC/KMS needs Redwood Dedicated or Private gives more control. Anthropic was mentioned 
similar, but for this POC we want to validate routing, KV cache, and prefix caching behavior which varies by provider.
[01:30] Ravi Patel: From infra side, we'll need VPC peering, SAML SSO, and integration with our KMS. Also audit logs retention and SOC 2  o you have a SOC 2 report we can share?
[01:41] Jordan Lee: Yes, we have SOC 2 and ISO docs 
d we'll share. For KMS, Redwood supports customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS) in Private and Dedicated.
[01:50] Priya Nair: Quick note on benchmarks 
d to emulate production we'll need: representative prompts, average prompt length, expected tokens per response, baseline QPS and peak concurrency. Can you share a two-week sample of anonymized logs?
[02:02] Evan Park: We can do that. I'll have infra extract anonymized call counts and average tokens.
[02:08] Samira Ortiz: Target SLA is 95th latency under 300ms for short queries (~<64 tokens) and 99th under 800ms for the UI path, like Evan said. Also quality acceptance: end-to-end extraction accuracy > 92% on a held-out prompt set.
[02:25] Priya Nair: Good, we'll set up scoring harness for structured extraction and run regression tests. We'll need a labeled eval set for that accuracy metric.
[02:34] Maya Chen: We have a small labeled set but it's only 400 examples. Is that sufficient?
[02:38] Priya Nair: It's okay to start; for statistical confidence we'll recommend at least 1k examples but POC can begin with 400 and expand during week 2.
[02:48] Jordan Lee: Now on integration: you mentioned you use an existing abstraction that hits OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Redwood supports an OpenAI-compatible API as an option and also our native SDKs in Python/TS. Which path do you prefer?
[03:00] Maya Chen: We prefer minimal changes 
d OpenAI-compatible endpoint would be easiest. But we also want function/tool calling and structured JSON outputs for downstream parsers. Does the OpenAI compat layer support function calling?
[03:12] Priya Nair: Yes, Redwood's OpenAI-compatible endpoints support function/tool calling. Small note: sometimes function schemas that are complex require slight adaptation 
d we can help map your tool schema. For more advanced routing and observability you might want to use the Redwood SDK which exposes tracing hooks.
[03:28] Samira Ortiz: For structured output we need eviction-safe KV caching between turns because we keep long conversation context; how's Redwood handling KV cache and streaming?
[03:38] Priya Nair: The runtime has KV cache management and supports streaming with incremental tokens. There's also prefix caching to speed up repeated prompts. Implementation details vary by model; we'll document best practices.
[03:49] Ravi Patel: On the Dedicated vs Hosted question, cost-wise what's the rough sizing if we expect baseline 20 qps and peaks at 120 qps during daytime? Median response size ~80 tokens.
[03:59] Jordan Lee: For an initial Dedicated reservation we typically recommend sizing for sustained QPS. For 20 sustained and 120 peak, a Dedicated pool with autoscale and burst capacity would cover it 
and we'll put exact GPU counts in the sizing template. For hosted, costs depend on per-token and concurrency; we'll run a cost simulation in the workbook.
[04:16] Priya Nair: We'll ask for two traffic profiles: a conservative sustained profile and a 99th percentile burst profile. We'll use both to calculate batch sizes, batching window, and expected latency distribution.
[04:26] Maya Chen: For the POC timeline, we were thinking 6 weeks: week 0 prep, week 1-2 ingest prompts and run bench, week 3 model tweaks, week 4 pilot with real traffic, week 5 rollback/analysis, week 6 decision. Is that realistic?
[04:38] Jordan Lee: Yep that's a common plan. We'll map responsibilities. Redwood will own benchmark harness and initial model suggestions; Nova owns providing prompt sets and infra for VPC peering if Dedicated/Private used.
[04:48] Evan Park: What about observability during POC? We need per-route latency, token cost, and per-token traceability.
[04:55] Leo Martinez: Redwood Console gives token-level breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and traces; we can give you a demo of the console and the tracing hooks. We'll also set up a shared metrics dashboard for the POC.
[05:05] Maya Chen: A couple technical nitpicks: do you support streaming structured JSON so our parser can handle partial tokens? And how deterministic is function calling when using multiple rolls/creative temperature?
[05:16] Priya Nair: Streaming JSON is supported but you need to handle partial chunks; we'll give sample client code for safe streaming parsing. For deterministic function calling, lower temp values and using schema/constrained decoding increase determinism. We also provide an automatic fallback policy when function calls fail.
[05:30] Samira Ortiz: For quality tests, can we run A/B between two model variants 
d faster quantized vs full-precision 
d to compare latency and accuracy?
[05:38] Priya Nair: Absolutely. Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization profiles per workload. We'll run parallel benchmarks and provide regression alerts if quality drops beyond a threshold.
[05:48] Jordan Lee: Ok let's capture acceptance criteria so we all agree. Proposed: 1) Latency: 95th <= 300ms for <64 token queries on interactive path; 2) Quality: structured extraction accuracy >= 92% on hold-out; 3) Cost: per-user token cost under the threshold you give us in the pricing spreadsheet; 4) Integration: OpenAI-compatible endpoint plus streaming structured output implemented in your app.
[06:08] Evan Park: That looks good, add security: SOC 2 and KMS integration must be validated in the POC.
[06:13] Jordan Lee: Noted. We'll include an Infosec checklist in the runbook.
[06:18] Maya Chen: For benchmarks, what's the harness? Are you using JMeter-like generator or a custom runner?
[06:24] Priya Nair: We use a custom runner that can replay real traces, vary token lengths, and measure token-level timing. We'll provide an initial harness and the spreadsheet to capture median/95/99 latency, throughput, token cost, success rate, function call success, and structured parse accuracy.
[06:41] Samira Ortiz: When we run distributed users hitting streaming endpoints, do you see connection limits? We have long-lived websockets for the app.
[06:48] Priya Nair: We support streaming via server-sent events and websockets depending on integration. We'll share recommended connection pooling and keepalive settings.
[06:56] Ravi Patel: Any limitations on number of concurrent connections per Dedicated node?
[07:00] Priya Nair: There are soft limits; we'll include them in the sizing doc. For large connection counts we recommend load balancers and pooling at app layer.
[07:07] Jordan Lee: Let's talk about function calling schema mapping 
d Maya, can you share an example of your expected function signatures?
[07:13] Maya Chen: Yes, our extraction function takes 'document_id', 'cursor', and returns a JSON block with fields: title, entities[], summary{short,long}, confidence. We also call an internal tool to enrich entity IDs.
[07:24] Priya Nair: We'll map that to Redwood function calling. Note: if the function schema nests arrays of objects with variable fields, it's best to define a strict JSON schema so the model knows the structure. We'll help with an automated schema validation step in the harness.
[07:37] Evan Park: On the model choice side, we might start with a smaller LLM variant to optimize cost but test a larger one for quality. Can you support switching models mid-POC without changing client code?
[07:48] Jordan Lee: Yes, with Redwood's routing and model abstraction you can pin a route to a model version or swap the backend; if you use the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, you'll change the model param. If you use the Redwood SDK, we can do rollouts and canary configs without client changes.
[08:02] Samira Ortiz: Regarding data retention, PII handling: can you scrub logs or turn off request logging?
[08:08] Jordan Lee: We can redact PII at ingestion and with Dedicated/Private you control retention policies. We'll document options 
d redaction, encryption at rest, and access controls.
[08:18] Maya Chen: For the POC, we want to capture high fidelity traces but with PII removed 
d is there a recommended pipeline for anonymization?
[08:25] Priya Nair: Yes, we can provide a redaction library in the SDK and a sample ETL that strips known fields before sending.
[08:33] Leo Martinez: I'll coordinate on the Console access 
d we'll give you a read-only dashboard and a shared metrics workspace.
[08:39] Evan Park: One more on contracts 
d if we move to Dedicated after POC, what's lead time to provision?
[08:45] Jordan Lee: Typically 2-4 weeks depending on GPU availability and region; for Private/on-prem it's longer 
d usually 6-12 weeks. We'll include options in the sizing doc.
[08:54] Maya Chen: For testing function calling failures, do you have built-in retry strategies?
[08:58] Priya Nair: Yes, we have configurable retry and fallback to a smaller stub or prompt-based fallback. We'll show the policies.
[09:07] Samira Ortiz: Ok, let's run through a sample bench plan quickly 
d week 1: replay traces against hosted OpenAI-compat endpoint, baseline latency; week 2: run Dedicated sim with same traces; week 3: A/B models and quantization; week 4: pilot with subset of production traffic; week 5: analyze and tune; week 6: decision and handoff.
[09:26] Jordan Lee: Sounds good. We'll also include regression criteria and alert thresholds in the workbook.
[09:31] Priya Nair: Action items 
d I'll create benchmark workbook and sample client code for streaming JSON and function calling. Jordan will send security docs and pricing. Nova will provide anonymized logs and labeled evals.
[09:44] Maya Chen: Quick note 
d we use an internal feature flagging system; during pilot we'll want toggle control to route users to Redwood or fallback. Does Redwood integrate with common feature flagging?
[09:54] Jordan Lee: We don't have native FF integration but you can implement route-level toggles in your app and Redwood routing can be controlled by the route header. We'll provide examples.
[10:03] Ravi Patel: For VPC peering we need network diagrams. Who provides that?
[10:07] Leo Martinez: We'll send network diagram templates and a runbook for peering.
[10:11] Evan Park: Ok let's recap who does what and dates:
[10:14] Jordan Lee: Recap: Redwood: send pricing, SOC2, network templates, console access; Priya: benchmark workbook by 4/20; Nova: logs by 4/18, labeled evals by 4/18; schedule Infosec runbook week of 4/27.
[10:31] Samira Ortiz: Great. Any blockers from Redwood side?
[10:35] Jordan Lee: None, just waiting on logs and the eval set. We'll follow up with Calendar invites for the benchmarks run.
[10:41] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone.
[10:45] Jordan Lee: Thanks all, we'll share the doc pack after the call.
